result.title: MSW: a Multi-Scale Sliced Wasserstein Distance Between Image Distributions
result.summary: We propose the multi-scale sliced Wasserstein (MSW) distance between image distributions, which operates in pixel space and requires no trained network. MSW convolves images with a fixed bank of discrete cosine filters at several scales, pools the responses over all positions, and compares the resulting one-dimensional distributions using the Wasserstein distance. We pair MSW with an exact two-sample test that gives calibrated p-values. Most metrics compare two image sets in the latent space of a pretrained network. We show that these metrics are insensitive to simple perturbations of the images, because the latent space is nearly invariant to them. In contrast, MSW detects smaller perturbations than latent-space metrics and needs far fewer images to do so. Although it uses no learned features, it still detects semantic changes of the image distribution. Finally, MSW matches or outperforms existing Wasserstein-based metrics in our experiments.

AI.brief_summary: 提出像素空间的 MSW 距离：用固定多尺度 DCT 滤波器组卷积图像、池化响应，再以一维 Wasserstein 距离比较图像分布，并配套精确两样本检验；实验称其比 latent 空间度量更敏感、所需样本更少，且仍能反映语义变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其免训练、像素空间分布距离与校准检验可供核查作为 LVR 中视觉细节保留及 latent 表征灵敏度的对照评价工具，但与推理状态生成机制无直接关系，迁移有效性需进一步确认。
